Continue a smooth, raised transfer toward the center with the tile retained; keep both arms on their own sides.
Bring the retained tile to a central presentation pose while beginning the right arm's raised receiving approach, without crossing wrists.
Settle the left-held tile near the center for handoff, keeping its grasp closed, while the right wrist rotates toward the receiving orientation.
Hold the tile steady in the left gripper and continue the right arm's slow receiving approach above the upright row.
Continue bringing the right receiver toward the held tile, keeping extra height to clear the row and the left fingers.

Rotate the retained tile gently about its center above the table, bringing its long dimension toward vertical while preserving grasp and joint continuity.
Continue the same slow center-preserving turn of the held end tile, keeping it elevated and separated from the upright row.
Complete most of the quarter-turn while compensating wrist translation so the retained tile stays clear of neighboring tiles.

Clear both open grippers from the arrangement for an unobstructed check; avoid touching the newly released end tile or the upright row.

Continue withdrawing the open arms to a clear viewing posture, preserving the completed tile arrangement.
Park the open right arm back from the table while retaining a small elbow bend. Leave the face-up kong and upright remaining tiles undisturbed.

Continue the high outer-side approach to the replacement, keeping the jaws open and clear of all upright tiles.
Align above the outer end tile for a precise final placement adjustment without touching its neighbors.
